title: Judge
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Hiro, a young man whose jealous lie led to his older brother's death, is abducted with eight others and held in an old courthouse, each wearing an animal mask tied to one of the seven deadly sins. Every twelve hours the captives must vote on which of them dies, and only four are promised release (Yen Press blurb via MangaUpdates; Fandom Post review).
life_message: Hidden guilt must be faced; under pressure people reveal who they are, and judging others is a trap.

content.note: Death-game executions by vote (Fandom Post; AniList Death Game, MU Murder/s). Gore level not described (to verify).
Bleak, tense, hopeless atmosphere (Fandom Post); AniList Survival, Battle Royale.
MU low-vote tags Attempted Rape, Seduction (to verify); lust is one of the sins.
Guilt over a brother's death (Yen Press blurb; MU Guilt).
Betrayal and deception as survival tactics (MU tags).

dominant: Sin, guilt and judgment; survival under coercion

frames.aligns: Seven deadly sins and the need to confess guilt.
frames.concerns: Captives judging and killing each other; judgment usurped from God.

frames.aligns: Repentance for Hiro's lie is central.
Sin has consequences; truth comes out.
frames.concerns: No grace offered in the setup; violence.

frames.aligns: Opens talk on sin, guilt and who may judge (Matthew 7:1).

frames.concerns: No gospel word; only law and death.

frames.aligns: Morality play framed around the deadly sins.
Refusing to kill would be the faithful choice.
Critique of scapegoating and mob judgment.
Craving and jealousy lead to suffering.

Five vices (lust, anger, greed, attachment, ego) as the frame.
Self-preservation tested; distrust of arbitrary authority.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Courtroom framing; votes replace personal duels (Fandom Post).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Captors impose strict rules; failing to vote kills all (Fandom Post).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Strangers forced together; a brother's death drives Hiro (blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Unseen captors hold total power over captives.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Seven deadly sins symbolism in a secular setting.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pure survival game (AniList Survival, MU Play or Die).

folkways.japan: Death-game stories are a popular Japanese thriller form, and public shame and guilt as drivers of punishment reflect familiar themes, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: Sin symbolism carries the theme; review notes no moralizing (Fandom Post) (to verify for later volumes).
delivery.note: The deadly sins serve as labels for each captive; the volumes reviewed leave the captors' motives unexplained.

winners_losers: Survivors who outlast the votes win; the story's sympathy goes to confronting guilt rather than to the captors' punitive judgment (to verify).
